newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Summers says IMF can sell gold and not hit market.
newsitem.headline: Summers says IMF can sell gold and not hit market.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Treasury Lawrence Summers said on Friday the International Monetary Fund can sell gold without an important effect on the gold market.
"We believe it would be possible to sell this gold without important effect on the gold market," Summers told a news conference in Singapore.

The IMF's board is to meet in Washington on Friday to discuss the sale of some five million ounces of its 104 million ounces of gold reserves over a period of time to bankroll debt relief for the world's poorest nations.
"If it is necessary to achieve adequate financing, the U.S. has indicated that it can support the sale of a limited amount of IMF gold," Summers told journalists.
He said that there had been previous IMF gold sales before and "based on historical experience" these had had little effect on the gold price.
